alt: A gallery in 2126 titled NFTs from the 2020s: three alcoves, each with a blank screen reading 404 Not Found, and one visitor looking at them
An NFT receipt in a wallet, with a dotted arrow labelled ask them pointing to a distant server in a shed, and an empty picture frame floating above it
A cheerful accountant in sleeve garters writing in an enormous ledger, while behind him a gallery of empty gilt frames stretches into the distance

A festival stage and crowd on the left; on the right a Festival Smart Contract checklist (artists, crew, production, venue, catering, security, suppliers) all ticked, with arrows paying each of them at once
A seller handing a framed painting to a delighted buyer while quietly feeding coins into a meter on the gallery wall

Two panels: on Bitcoin, a sealed, padlocked time capsule that nothing can act on, with a shrugging bystander; on Stacks, the same capsule opened, a friendly robot reading the letter, a tick stamping it unaltered and a machine acting on it
The error message in off-white monospace on dark charcoal: cloud_name chemical-x is disabled
The ThisIsNumberOne (V2) collection page on Gamma in a wide view: two long rows of blank grey tiles, with only Hash One #44, #76 and #86 still loading, marked with orange arrows
A film still leading to a film reel, which splits into a working IPFS copy with a green tick and a Cloudinary copy that has gone, with a cross

Bar chart of the 241 art collections by status: 1 on chain, 26 healthy, 173 fragile (works today, but one host away from not working), 6 marketplace copy broken, 16 walking dead (the contract's link is dead but the marketplace still shows a copy), 5 failing, 13 lost and 1 unclear, with a bracket marking the 34 walking dead, failing and lost

A wide dusk street scene in navy, orange and cream: a man lights the lawn of a large house with a lamp powered by a long orange extension lead, which runs the whole length of the garden and through a neighbour's gate to a plug in the neighbour's garage
Thirteen file icons with arrows converging on a single JSON file, behind whose door a website homepage looks puzzled
Ape Club artwork linked to several working hosts, against Robots artwork linked to a single server wearing a Service Suspended sign
Where the art lives: IPFS, 203 collections, 4 broken (2%); own server or API, 16 collections, 9 broken (56%)
The gateway that closed: a stone toll-gate marked Closed, 14 Aug 2024, with three framed artworks stranded at the barrier while the rest walk round by a side track marked other hosts
Broken, by year deployed: 28% for 2021 (23 of 81), 8% for 2022 (7 of 90), 0% for 2023 to 2024 (0 of 42), 17% for 2025 (2 of 12), two of which were deployed in October 2025 and are already lost
A candle-lit dining room, immaculately laid, while through the swing doors the kitchen is a bare empty room with no stove, and a nervous waiter looks on
Stacks Punks V3, one file for everyone: a grid of generic pixel portraits all pointing at one punks.json card showing a single picture, and a man scratching his head asking who is number 4,812
A friendly look over the fence: a neighbour with a mug of tea waving at a row of sheds labelled Ethereum, Base, Polygon, Arbitrum and Tezos

Three objects drawn to scale with the cost to put each on chain: a tiny pixel bird (3 to 8 KB, about 0.02 STX), an album-style image (about 1.8 MB, 2 to 5 STX) and a huge film reel (258 MB, around 400 STX)

How a twin works: an original token whose image is not stored on chain, a helper contract holding a sealed record of the file's hash, size and type, and a twin token holding the actual file chunks, with a tick showing the bytes match and a two-way swap between original and twin

The five Genesis pieces on Gamma, with their artists: Channel #1 by Orbital, This Is Number One by Chemical X, So Why Try Harder by Fatboy Slim, Now Is Not Enough by Dave Stewart and Mine by Cara Delevingne
A stone cathedral labelled the chain on a hill, with a scatter of rented sheds, a pin-board, a water tank and a van around it, each carrying a rent notice, with artworks stored inside
What to do on Monday: a planner page with a ticked checklist beside a laptop showing a wallet address and a green tick, and a mug of coffee
